description: Capability for the main window. Least privilege on purpose: the only filesystem paths the app touches are `$APPDATA/images` (product covers: read, write, mkdir) and `$APPLOCALDATA/logs` (the log file the Setting > Log page reads and clears). The commands enabled are exactly the ones `src/lib/image.ts` and `src/services/log/live.ts` call — `fs:read-files` (exists, read_file, read_text_file) and `fs:write-files` (write_file, write_text_file, remove) scoped to those two paths, plus `fs:allow-mkdir` for the images folder, whose path scope comes from the same allow-lists. `fs:default` is deliberately NOT granted: it adds `read-app-specific-dirs-recursive`, i.e. recursive read of every app-specific directory — including the one holding `sqlite:data.db`, the Tauri store and the logs — which no frontend call needs. The JSON exports do not go through the fs plugin: they call the Rust `export_file` command, which opens the save dialog and writes the file itself, so a user-picked path never needs to be inside this scope. `core:webview:allow-set-webview-zoom` is what the Setting > Tampilan zoom slider calls (`getCurrentWebview().setZoom()`), and nothing else in the app rescales the webview. `core:window:allow-destroy` is granted for one caller: `useFlushOnExit` closes the window itself once the cart is on disk. Tauri's Rust side calls `prevent_close()` as soon as a JS listener sits on `tauri://close-requested`, so from the moment the app started listening for closes this side had to destroy the window — and `core:window:default` does not include `destroy`, which the API's own listener calls for you. Refused, silently, inside that listener: the app could not be quit at all. `sql:allow-execute` is the one deliberate hole — the SQLite access layer runs statements issued by `src/services/db` — and it is compensated by the window CSP below.
